title: Phase 4: Media Upload & Management
description:
## Overview
Implement full media upload pipeline with Cloudflare R2 storage, including image/video processing and a media library UI.

## Tasks
- [ ] Set up Cloudflare R2 bucket and credentials
- [ ] Create presigned URL generation for direct uploads
- [ ] Build upload processing pipeline (thumbnails, optimization)
- [ ] Implement media library UI with grid view
- [ ] Add drag-and-drop upload support
- [ ] Create video player component with controls
- [ ] Add image optimization (resize, compress)
- [ ] Generate video thumbnails

## Technical Details

### R2 Upload Flow
1. Client requests presigned URL from API
2. Client uploads directly to R2
3. Webhook/callback triggers processing
4. Thumbnails generated, metadata stored in DB
5. Media appears in library

### API Endpoints Needed
- POST /api/media/upload-url - Get presigned URL
- POST /api/media/complete - Mark upload complete, trigger processing
- GET /api/media - List user's media
- DELETE /api/media/[id] - Remove media

### Processing Pipeline
- Images: Generate thumbnails (300px, 600px), compress original
- Videos: Extract thumbnail at 1s, store duration/dimensions

## Acceptance Criteria
- Drag files to upload area, see progress
- Images auto-optimize and generate thumbnails
- Videos extract thumbnail automatically
- Media library shows all uploads with filtering
- Can select media to add to portfolio sections

## Dependencies
- Requires R2 credentials configured
- Phase 1 database schema (media table exists)

title: Epic: Site Export for Self-Hosting
description:
Allow users to export their complete portfolio site as a downloadable package they can self-host on any static hosting platform (GitHub Pages, Netlify, personal server, etc.).

## Goals
- Provide a one-click export that produces a fully functional standalone website
- Include all media assets (images, videos) in the export
- Support both HTML-based and JSON-based portfolio types
- Generate self-contained HTML that requires no backend
- Provide deployment documentation for common platforms

## User Story
As a portfolio owner, I want to export my entire site so I can host it on my own domain/server without depending on the platform.

## Success Criteria
- Export produces valid ZIP file with complete site
- Exported site works when served from any static HTTP server
- All images/videos are included and display correctly
- Contact forms degrade gracefully (mailto: fallback or form service)
- Export includes README with deployment instructions

title: Design export API endpoint structure
description:
Design the API endpoint for portfolio export.

## Endpoint
`POST /api/portfolios/[id]/export`

## Requirements
- Authenticate user owns the portfolio
- Accept options parameter for export configuration:
  - `includeVideos`: boolean (videos can be large)
  - `embedFonts`: boolean (embed Google Fonts vs CDN links)
  - `format`: 'zip' | 'tar.gz'
- Return streaming response for ZIP download
- Set appropriate headers (Content-Disposition, Content-Type)

## Response
- Content-Type: application/zip
- Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="portfolio-export.zip"
- Streaming body with ZIP content

## Error Cases
- 401: Not authenticated
- 403: User doesn't own portfolio
- 404: Portfolio not found
- 500: Export generation failed

## Considerations
- Large exports may timeout - consider background job + download link pattern for portfolios with many videos
- Rate limiting to prevent abuse

title: Implement ZIP packaging service
description:
Create service to package all export components into a downloadable ZIP file.

## Requirements
- Create ZIP with proper directory structure
- Stream ZIP creation for memory efficiency
- Support large media files without loading all into memory
- Set proper file permissions in ZIP

## Implementation
- Create `lib/export/packager.ts`
- Use `archiver` npm package for ZIP creation
- Function: `createExportPackage(data: ExportPackage): ReadableStream`

## Package Structure
```
portfolio-export.zip
├── index.html              # Main site
├── manifest.json           # Portfolio metadata
├── README.md              # Deployment instructions
├── assets/
│   ├── styles.css         # If separated
│   └── fonts/
│       ├── fonts.css
│       └── *.woff2
└── media/
    ├── images/
    │   └── *.jpg, *.png, *.webp
    └── videos/
        └── *.mp4, *.webm
```

## Dependencies
- `archiver` or `jszip` npm package

## Streaming
```typescript
const archive = archiver('zip', { zlib: { level: 6 } })
archive.append(htmlContent, { name: 'index.html' })
archive.directory('media/', 'media')
return archive
```

title: Add export analytics and rate limiting
description:
Track export usage and prevent abuse.

## Analytics
Track in database or analytics service:
- Export initiated (portfolioId, userId, timestamp)
- Export completed (success/failure, file size, duration)
- Export options used (videos included, fonts embedded)

## Rate Limiting
- Limit exports per user: 10 per day
- Limit export file size: 500MB max
- Return 429 if rate limit exceeded with retry-after header

## Implementation
```typescript
// Check rate limit before export
const recentExports = await db
  .select()
  .from(exportLogs)
  .where(and(
    eq(exportLogs.userId, userId),
    gt(exportLogs.createdAt, dayAgo)
  ))

if (recentExports.length >= 10) {
  return new Response('Rate limit exceeded', { status: 429 })
}
```

## Database Schema Addition
```sql
CREATE TABLE export_logs (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id uuid REFERENCES users(id),
  portfolio_id uuid REFERENCES portfolios(id),
  file_size bigint,
  include_videos boolean,
  embed_fonts boolean,
  status text, -- 'started', 'completed', 'failed'
  error_message text,
  created_at timestamp DEFAULT now(),
  completed_at timestamp
);
```

title: Implement font embedding for offline use
description:
Handle Google Fonts to ensure exported sites work offline.

## Problem
AI-generated HTML portfolios use Google Fonts (Space Grotesk, Instrument Serif, etc.) loaded from CDN. For true self-hosting, fonts should be embedded.

## Options
1. **Embed fonts** - Download font files, include in export
2. **Keep CDN links** - Simpler, requires internet connection
3. **User choice** - Let user decide via export options

## Implementation
- Create `lib/export/font-handler.ts`
- Parse HTML for Google Fonts links
- Download font files (.woff2) from Google Fonts CSS
- Generate local `assets/fonts.css` with @font-face rules
- Rewrite HTML to use local font CSS

## Font Extraction
1. Find: `<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=...">`
2. Fetch CSS, parse @font-face rules
3. Download each .woff2 file
4. Generate local CSS pointing to downloaded files
5. Replace Google Fonts link with local CSS

## Output
```
assets/
└── fonts/
    ├── fonts.css
    ├── space-grotesk-400.woff2
    ├── space-grotesk-700.woff2
    └── instrument-serif-400.woff2
```

   - [ ] Embed fonts for offline use

## Implementation
```tsx
// components/dashboard/export-button.tsx
export function ExportButton({ portfolioId }: { portfolioId: string }) {
  const [isExporting, setIsExporting] = useState(false)
  const [showOptions, setShowOptions] = useState(false)
  
  const handleExport = async (options: ExportOptions) => {
    setIsExporting(true)
    const response = await fetch(`/api/portfolios/${portfolioId}/export`, {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify(options)
    })
    // Trigger download from blob
    const blob = await response.blob()
    downloadBlob(blob, 'portfolio-export.zip')
  }
}
```

## States
- Idle: Show "Export Site" button
- Options: Show modal with checkboxes
- Exporting: Show spinner with "Preparing export..."
- Complete: Auto-download, show success message
